topics.name: Question tags (I am, let's, there, nobody, commands)
Wh-questions to get a given answer

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Della was very poor, was she?
Della was very poor, wasn't she?
Della was very poor, didn't she?
questions.rule: A positive sentence with was takes a negative tag with the same helper: wasn't she?

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct infinitive.
options: Della wanted to buy a gift for Jim.
Della wanted to bought a gift for Jim.
Della wanted buying a gift for Jim.
questions.rule: want is followed by the infinitive to + base verb: wanted to buy.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: spend time is followed by the -ing form: spent hours counting.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The simple past sold uses 'did', so the tag is didn't he?

questions.prompt: Complete the short answer.
questions.before: Have you cut off your hair? Yes, I
questions.rule: A short answer repeats the helper verb of the question: Have you ...? Yes, I have.

questions.prompt: Fill in the gap.
questions.after: books is good for the mind.
questions.rule: A gerund (Reading) can be the subject of a sentence.

questions.prompt: Make a suggestion with a question tag.
questions.rule: A sentence beginning with Let's takes the tag shall we?

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply.
options: Yes, I will. Take your hat off.
Yes, I do. Take your hat off.
Yes, I am. Take your hat off.
questions.rule: Answer a Will you ...? question with Yes, I will / No, I won't.

questions.prompt: Frame a wh-question to get the words 'At 7 o'clock'.
questions.source: At 7 o'clock the coffee was made.
questions.rule: Ask about time with When + helper + subject: When was the coffee made?

questions.prompt: Add a question tag.
options: They were expensive combs, didn't they?
They were expensive combs, were they?
They were expensive combs, weren't they?
questions.rule: Positive were takes the negative tag weren't they?

questions.prompt: Pick the correct short answer to 'Can you afford it?'
questions.rule: Repeat the helper of the question: Can you ...? No, I can't.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: If Della did not sell her hair, she could not have bought the chain.
If Della had not sold her hair, she could not bought the chain.
If Della had not sold her hair, she could not have bought the chain.
questions.rule: Third conditional: If + had + past participle, could/would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After did use the base verb: Where did Della go?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The -ing participle describes what causes the feeling: a terrifying moment.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct question tag.
questions.before: I am the luckiest girl in town,
questions.rule: The tag for I am is aren't I?

questions.prompt: Fill in the gap.
questions.after: did Della pay for the fob chain?
questions.rule: Money is uncountable, so ask How much.

questions.prompt: Make a question.
questions.rule: Wh-word + did + subject + base verb: Why did Della sell ...?

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply.
options: Yes! The ending was a big surprise, didn't it?
Yes! The ending was a big surprise, wasn't it?
Yes! The ending was a big surprise, was it?
questions.rule: Positive was takes the negative tag wasn't it?

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply.
questions.rule: Are you ...? takes the short answer No, I'm not. 'Amn't' is not standard English.

questions.prompt: Frame a wh-question to get the words 'below her knee'.
questions.source: Her hair reached below her knee.
questions.rule: Ask about place with Where did + subject + base verb (reach).

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Give it to me quickly, do you?
Give it to me quickly, will you?
Give it to me quickly, won't it?
questions.rule: A command takes the tag will you?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The tag for I am is always aren't I?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: start takes a gerund or an infinitive: started curling.

questions.prompt: Fill in the gap.
questions.before: Had Jim known about the hair, he
questions.rule: Third conditional result: would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: Fill in the gap.
questions.rule: After a preposition (of) use a gerund: fond of looking.

questions.prompt: Make a third conditional sentence.
questions.rule: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply.
chat: I finished 'The Gift of the Magi' last night.
options: Really? What did Jim give Della?
Really? What did Jim gave Della?
questions.rule: Question order: What + did + subject + base verb: What did Jim give ...?

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply.
chat: Do you think Della should have waited a few days?
options: If she had waited, she would not have bought anything.
If she waited, she would not have bought anything.
If she had waited, she would not had bought anything.
questions.rule: Third conditional: If she had waited, she would not have bought ...

questions.prompt: Add a question tag.
questions.source: There was clearly nothing to do.
options: There was clearly nothing to do, wasn't there?
There was clearly nothing to do, was it?
There was clearly nothing to do, was there?
questions.rule: Nothing makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive; 'there' repeats: was there?

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Infinitive = to + base verb (buy); the story is past: decided; Hardly pairs with when.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct short answer to 'Does it make any difference?'
questions.rule: Does it ...? takes No, it doesn't; 'it' needs 'does', not 'do'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
options: Had Della kept her hair, the combs will have looked lovely on her.
Had Della kept her hair, the combs would have looked lovely on her.
If had Della kept her hair, the combs would have looked lovely on her.
questions.rule: Had + subject + past participle replaces 'If ... had'; the result needs would have.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: After did use the base verb: did Della have?

questions.prompt: Complete the short answer.
questions.before: Isn't it a dandy? Yes, it
questions.rule: A 'yes' short answer is positive: Yes, it is. 'Yes' never goes with 'isn't'.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence with an infinitive.
questions.rule: want + to + base verb: wanted to surprise.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply.
options: Playing the sitar is my hobby.
Play the sitar is my hobby.
To playing the sitar is my hobby.
questions.rule: A gerund (Playing the sitar) can be the subject of a sentence.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply.
chat: O. Henry always ends his stories with a surprise.
options: Yes! Everyone loves a surprise, aren't they?
Yes! Everyone loves a surprise, don't they?
Yes! Everyone loves a surprise, isn't it?
questions.rule: After everyone the tag uses they; 'loves' is simple present, so don't they?

questions.prompt: Frame a wh-question to get the words 'for Jim's present'.
questions.source: She was ransacking the stores for Jim's present.
options: What she was ransacking the stores for?
What was she ransacking the stores for?
What was she ransacking the stores?
questions.rule: Helper before subject (was she), and keep the preposition: ... the stores for?

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Third conditional: had known, had not sold, and would have used.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: keep on and feel like take the -ing form: kept on smiling, felt like crying.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct question tag.
options: Nobody could count Della's love, could they?
Nobody could count Della's love, couldn't they?
Nobody could count Della's love, couldn't it?
questions.rule: Nobody makes the sentence negative, so the tag is positive and uses they: could they?

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Third conditional result: would not have + past participle (sold).

questions.prompt: Fill in the gap.
questions.after: the price, Della hurried home with the eighty-seven cents.
questions.rule: A perfect participle (Having paid) shows the first of two actions by the same person.

questions.prompt: Make a sentence beginning with 'Had'.
questions.rule: Had + subject + past participle = 'If she had known'; then would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: Pick the correct reply.
chat: Della sold her hair for twenty dollars.
options: To whom did she sell it?
Whom did she sold it to?
questions.rule: Question order: To whom + did + subject + base verb: To whom did she sell it?

questions.prompt: Give a short positive answer.
questions.source: Don't you like me any more?
questions.rule: A short answer uses pronoun + helper: Yes, I do. 'Yes' needs a positive helper.

questions.prompt: Begin the sentence with 'Had'.
questions.source: If Jim had come home early, he would have seen Della's long hair.
options: Had Jim came home early, he would have seen Della's long hair.
Had Jim come home early, he would see Della's long hair.
Had Jim come home early, he would have seen Della's long hair.
questions.rule: Drop 'If' and put Had first; keep the past participle come and would have seen.

questions.prompt: Frame a wh-question to get the words 'sobs, sniffles and smiles'.
questions.source: Life is made up of sobs, sniffles and smiles.
options: What is life made up of?
What does life made up of?
questions.rule: Helper before subject (is life) and keep the whole phrase: made up of?

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: 'came ... and stopped' are both past; too ... to + base verb (say); Had he known.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Past story: cried; infinitive to buy; plural They both takes were.
